T0651.title: Digital Human
T0651.definition: A digital human is a virtual character with a computer-generated appearance and interactive behavior produced through graphics, motion driving, speech synthesis, and artificial intelligence technologies.
T0651.description:
A digital human commonly combines character modeling, rendering, motion capture or generation, speech synthesis, lip synchronization, and conversational models. It may serve as a virtual presenter, customer-service agent, brand representative, instructor, or social character. Digital humans can be driven by a person, rules, or AI and can use photorealistic, cartoon, or stylized appearances.

In business-security contexts, the technology can reduce livestreaming, service, and content-production costs, but it can also support impersonation, undisclosed synthetic identities, deceptive livestream sales, mass-produced marketing content, or emotional fraud. Risk analysis should distinguish the neutral concept of a digital human from the tools that generate one and from concrete fraud conducted through one.
T0651.usageExample: The platform requires each Digital Human livestream to disclose its synthetic identity and verify authorization for the likeness, voice, and operating organization.
